gaps.sentence: While the chef ___ the sauce, the waiter set the tables.
gaps.hint: while frames the longer simultaneous action
gaps.explanation: 'While' frames the longer simultaneous action, which takes the past continuous: was preparing.

gaps.sentence: My back hurts because I ___ the garden all afternoon.
gaps.hint: all afternoon explains the present pain
gaps.explanation: A recent continuous activity with a visible present result takes the present perfect continuous: have been digging.

gaps.sentence: By the time I woke up, my flatmates ___ to work.
gaps.hint: by the time plus past simple
gaps.explanation: 'By the time' plus a past action refers back to an earlier past action, so the past perfect is needed: had gone.

gaps.sentence: Don't disturb him — he ___ an important video call with the client.
gaps.hint: do not disturb means it is happening now
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous: is having.

gaps.sentence: The moon ___ round the Earth roughly every 27 days.
gaps.hint: a timeless fact about the moon
gaps.explanation: Timeless facts take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: Shakespeare ___ thirty-seven plays that we know of.
gaps.hint: a dead historical figure, finished lifetime
gaps.explanation: Actions of people who are no longer alive take the past simple even without a time phrase: wrote.

gaps.sentence: The bus ___ at 6.40 tomorrow morning, according to the timetable.
gaps.hint: official timetables use the present simple
gaps.explanation: Official timetables take the present simple for future events: leaves.

gaps.sentence: I ___ her at a conference in 2019, but we did not start working together until last year.
gaps.hint: in 2019 pins a finished past time
gaps.explanation: 'In 2019' is a finished past time, so the past simple is required: met.
